summary: CCC-built L-4 lookout of 1938 on Silver Peak in Cochise County, AZ; NRHP-listed 1988; burned around 1996, leaving ruins, a storage shed and a water cache.

facts.design: L-4 type lookout, wood frame, 14 by 14 feet, with an outhouse, storage shed and water cistern
facts.status_note: Tower burned around 1996 per Ominous; ruins of the tower, a locked storage shed and an old water cache remain on the site
facts.agency: Coronado National Forest, Douglas Ranger District

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as an L-4 type lookout
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places January 28, 1988
Tower burned down around 1996 during a thunder-snowstorm, per Ominous; the year is approximate

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Ominous gives the place as Paradise, Arizona; the National Register record gives Portal vicinity, Cochise County. The story uses the register's wording for the place and notes the disagreement.

sources.title: Silver Peak Lookout Complex - Paradise, Arizona

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination PDF (NARA copy) and the Living New Deal page both returned 403 and were not read. The 1938 CCC build date and the c.1996 fire rest on Ominous, a user-run listing site; check both against the nomination before publishing. No staffing, fire history or public-access information was found, so no access fact is recorded. The brief's county (Cochise) is correct. The OpenStreetMap entry tags the site as ruins, which fits the fate.
